meta.purpose: The HTTP endpoint surface of both platforms, as queryable data. Endpoints only: trigger, request contract, responses, error handling, and the resources each touches. Action-level configuration is not here — it is printed verbatim, per action, on the provisioning pages under docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/provisioning/flows/.

capture.limit: The export uses the maker cmdlet Get-Flow, which returns only flows the exporting account owns or co-owns. A flow owned solely by another person is absent from this dataset and nothing here would know. These figures describe what the export found, not what the environment contains. Obtain an administrative inventory (Get-AdminFlow) before treating any count here as complete.

conventions.nullMeansNotDeclared: A null field means the package does not declare the value. Where the distinction matters a sibling boolean (…Declared) states it explicitly, because an absent authentication posture and a posture of "All" are different facts.
conventions.normalisation: endpoints[] are contract keys; flows[] are the definitions behind them, referenced by id. Several keys share one flow, so a key may name a flow another key also names.
conventions.credentials: No trigger URL appears in this file. A signed URL is a bearer credential; the workflow id it addresses is not, and is what is recorded.
conventions.identifiers: A flow carries two ids and they are not interchangeable. flowId is the dashed GUID Power Automate names the flow by — it is what the maker portal URL carries, every export records it, and all flows here have one. workflowId is the 32-hex id a SIGNED TRIGGER URL addresses; NO PACKAGE IN THIS TREE CARRIES IT (every export records full_resource_id as null), so it is joined from the two registers and left null where no register names the flow. Never treat one as the other. captureId is neither — it is this dataset's own row key, the export filename, needed because one flowId is carried by two differing captures.
conventions.lookup: index at the foot of this file maps an id to the POSITION of the row holding it, so a consumer with no filtering of its own — a Power Automate expression, for one — reaches a row directly instead of scanning. Values are lists of zero-based positions into the array the key prefix names; the rows themselves are never repeated there. See docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/reference/ENDPOINTS_JSON_IN_POWER_AUTOMATE.md.
conventions.makerUrl: flowMakerUrl is CONSTRUCTED by this generator from environmentName and flowId, both verbatim from the package. It is not a value read from anything, and it is flagged flowMakerUrlIsConstructed on every row that carries one.
